research_notes: No current evidence suggests scheduler pre-arm itself is the limiting factor in this strict sample.
The experimental question remains how long useful work can continue while preserving normal durable close.
Because the wake is already secured, a late failure primarily risks the newest work/checkpoint rather than total relay continuity.
That architecture may support a more aggressive operating cap than a design that rearms only at the end, but validation is still required.
A clean 14m close would be the next incremental lower-bound observation, not the final answer.
The next invocation should not skip retrospective wake reconciliation before launching 16m.
